problem:
The center of the hyperbola $\frac{(x-13)^{2}}{49}-\frac{(y-6)^{2}}{64}=1$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(x-13)^{2}}{49}-\frac{(y-6)^{2}}{64}=1
$$

In this case, $h=13$ and $k=6.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,13,6\,).$
